setup.inputs: requestAuthorityLifecycleInputs = { base: ephemeral loopback origin, phase: application | request | survivor | independent }
ordering: GET /body returns real chunked HTTP headers and first chunk 'first'; all remaining bytes withheld
JS receives headers, reads first chunk, starts next read, then GET /ready?pending=true
application: host revokes application only after /ready receipt; invocation rejects before body release
request: host cancels invocation after /ready receipt (native drops evaluation future; Core uses invoke AbortSignal); invocation does not return
request: next serial invocation denies retained handle and reader then GET /fresh succeeds
independent: a different admitted application and VM realm completes GET /fresh while A remains pending at /ready; only then revoke A and await rejection
independent: B completes a second GET /fresh after A revocation; both probes see no A retained globals and only frozen opaque fs/http
release held connection only after invocation settles; check empty resources and bounded graceful shutdown before export
setup.ownership: Native-only held request environments prove context ownership. Serial survivor proves same-scope cross-request isolation. Separate admitted applications and real VM realms prove cross-isolate in-flight independence, with B invoked while A is suspended and again after A revocation.
limits: Native request cancellation drops the executing evaluation future; Core request cancellation aborts the host invoke signal.
Held A/B context revocation is a separate host ownership check, not cancellation of the executing streaming request.
Opacity checks test supplied trusted context strings, not an invented provider or secret API.
No physical qualification, OS security, simultaneous CPU execution, or same-isolate parallel JS claim.
